$comment: What a project's `cache.handler` `read()` answer means, and what a host does with it.
Three implementations hold this rule and cannot share code: `handleDocumentRead` in
`packages/ruvyxa/runtime/worker-pool.mjs` normalizes the answer for the Axum host,
`normalizeCacheEntry` in `packages/ruvyxa/runtime/serverless-handler.mjs` normalizes it for
every deployed build, and `stored_document_from_response` + `serve_stored_document` in
`crates/ruvyxa_dev_server/src/render_pipeline.rs` interpret the worker's answer and decide
what to serve. They drifted twice before this file existed: the worker called a bare string
fresh while the deployed handler called it stale, and the Rust host treated a stale document
as a miss — falling through to the build's own document, which is older — while the deployed
host served it and refreshed behind the response.
`answers`: a raw `read()` answer, the wire shape the worker emits for it (`html` is `null` for a
miss and the `stale` key is then absent), and what it means. `serving`: given a normalized
document and the route's strategy, whether the host serves it and whether an ISR route refreshes
it behind the response. A miss is served by neither host — the deployed host renders, the Axum
host falls back to the build's directory and then renders. PPR is a stored shell like SSG and
CSR — its dynamic slots fill in client-side on hydration — so it is served and never refreshed;
the deployed host used to render it in full on every request while still writing the forced
render to a store it never read.
Replayed by `reads and writes stored documents through cache.handler` and
`normalizes every store answer the fixture lists` in `tests/packages/ruvyxa/worker-pool.test.mjs`,
by `stored document conformance` in `tests/packages/ruvyxa/serverless-handler.test.mjs`, and by
`stored_document_conformance` in `crates/ruvyxa_dev_server/src/render_pipeline.rs`.

answers.name: a bare string is a document whose freshness the store did not state, so it is stale
an object that says fresh is fresh
an object that says stale is held, not missing
an object with no flag is fresh
an object whose html is not a string is a miss whatever the flag says
an object with no html is a miss

serving.name: a miss under ISR is rendered, not served
a fresh document under ISR is served and left alone
a stale document under ISR is served and refreshed behind the response
a miss under SSG is rendered, not served
a fresh document under SSG is served
a stale document under SSG is served; there is no window to refresh against
a stale document under CSR is served; there is no window to refresh against
a miss under PPR is rendered, not served
a fresh shell under PPR is served
a stale shell under PPR is served; there is no window to refresh against
